InstanceType.issue: HeistPower.cs:15 PowerInstanceType.Instanced -- the audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json G5 mechanism, cross-referenced under rule 3. DORMANT here: the only applier is SurprisePower applying one HeistPower to the one Fat Gremlin it spawns (powers.py:1698ff), so two simultaneous instances are unreachable. Eleventh PowerInstanceType unit -- see the note on power/thievery.

BeforeDeath.issue: HOOK-PHASE MISMATCH -- a BEFORE hook ported onto an AFTER hook, the recurring shape section 0 item 5 of the stream report names for thorns/curl_up/skittish/suck, now in a death-time form. C# calls Hook.BeforeDeath UNCONDITIONALLY at CreatureCmd.cs:503, two lines BEFORE Hook.ShouldDie at :505 decides whether the death stands. The sim's on_death fires only INSIDE the should_die-true branch (cmds.py:96-105), i.e. it is AfterDeath (CreatureCmd.cs:519), not BeforeDeath. Two divergences follow: (a) when a listener prevents the death, C# has already queued the GoldReward and the sim has not; and (b) if the creature is later killed for real, C# calls BeforeDeath a SECOND time and queues the reward TWICE. DORMANT, established by enumerating the ported should_die listeners rather than by assertion: they are IllusionPower (powers.py:1566), SteamEruptionPower (:2016), AdaptablePower (:3365), FairyInABottle (potions.py:1242, player-only) and Lizard Tail (relics/lizard_tail.py:35, player-only). The three enemy ones are self-buffs on Hive and Glory monsters; HeistPower's owner is the Underdocks Fat Gremlin that SurprisePower spawns, and nothing applies a death-preventer to it. Named trigger: any ported effect that prevents a Fat Gremlin's death, or applying Illusion/Adaptable cross-act.

guards.rationale: Run-history bookkeeping for the end-of-run screen, with no gameplay reader; the sim has no history entry to mark. Waiver: presentation. Note it is OUTSIDE C#'s CombatRoom type test (:23-26) and so runs even when the reward is not queued -- which the sim cannot diverge on, having neither.

The sim appends RewardExtra.of_gold(self.amount) to combat.pending_reward_extras (powers.py:1684-1685), documented at rewards.py:363 as the wasGoldStolenBack port. Same amount, same single-player recipient, same reward-screen destination.

guards.what: powers.py:1679 the sim ADDS an amount <= 0 test
guards.rationale: A GUARD THE SIM ADDS (bug class 8) that turns out to be LOAD-BEARING COMPENSATION, which is why it is faithful rather than a divergence. C# has no such test, so on its face a zero-amount HeistPower would queue a GoldReward(0) in the game and nothing in the sim -- and a zero amount is very reachable (kill the Merc before it ever attacks, so ThieveryPower's total is 0 and SurprisePower moves 0 across). But C#'s PowerCmd.Apply returns early on amount == 0m (PowerCmd.cs:104), so the game never creates the power at all and never reaches BeforeDeath. The sim has no zero-amount no-op -- that is power_cmd's step-6 finding, confirmed here by reading cmds.py:288-326 -- so it DOES create HeistPower(0), and this added guard is what makes the two sides agree. Recorded because the guard must not be removed independently of fixing power_cmd step 6: either alone is correct, neither-or-both is a divergence.

guards.what: HeistPower.cs:23 the CombatRoom type test, and the escape path
guards.rationale: C# queues the reward only if CurrentRoom is a CombatRoom; the sim's on_death reaches combat.pending_reward_extras only from inside a combat, so the test is structurally satisfied. The sim's docstring claim that escape never fires BeforeDeath is correct and matters: a Fat Gremlin that flees is removed without CreatureCmd.Kill, so neither side pays the gold back.
